subject: AP Biology
stem: Water has a much higher specific heat than most other molecules of similar size. Which explanation best accounts for this property?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Much of the heat added to water is used to break hydrogen bonds between water molecules before the molecules can move faster.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The covalent bonds inside each water molecule must break before the temperature of the water can rise.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Water molecules are nonpolar, so they absorb heat without interacting with one another.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Liquid water is dense, so heat is trapped between tightly packed molecules.

rationales.A: Raising the temperature means making molecules move faster. In water, much of the absorbed energy first goes into breaking hydrogen bonds between molecules, so more heat is needed for each degree of change. Tracing the property back to polarity and hydrogen bonding is what earns the point.
rationales.B: Tempts because 'breaking bonds absorbs energy' sounds right, but heating water does not break the covalent O-H bonds inside each molecule. Fix: the bonds that absorb the heat are hydrogen bonds between molecules, not covalent bonds within one.
rationales.C: Tempts because it sounds like a simple reason for absorbing heat, but water is polar, and that polarity is the reason it has a high specific heat at all. Fix: start every water-property answer from 'water is polar'.
rationales.D: Tempts because density is another well-known property of water, but density does not explain how much heat water absorbs per degree. Fix: name the mechanism for the property asked about, which here is hydrogen bonds absorbing energy.

earned: Start from polarity: water is polar.
Name hydrogen bonds between molecules as the cause.
Finish with the biological consequence of the property.
lost: Naming a property with no molecular cause.
Confusing hydrogen bonds with covalent bonds.
Explaining one property with the mechanism of another.

subject: AP Biology
stem: The concentration of glucose inside an intestinal epithelial cell is higher than in the intestinal lumen, yet the cell keeps taking up glucose from the lumen through a membrane protein. Which statement best describes this uptake?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Facilitated diffusion, because a membrane protein carries the glucose.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Simple diffusion, because glucose moves into the cell where it is used.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Active transport, because glucose moves from lower to higher concentration, which requires an energy input.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Osmosis, because water follows glucose into the cell.

rationales.A: Tempts because a protein is involved, but proteins carry out active transport too; a carrier alone does not make movement passive. Fix: decide passive or active from the gradient direction, not from whether a protein is present.
rationales.B: Tempts because the cell uses the glucose, but diffusion only moves a substance from higher to lower concentration, and glucose cannot cross the bilayer on its own. Fix: check the gradient direction before naming diffusion.
rationales.C: Glucose moves from the lumen, where its concentration is lower, into the cell, where it is higher, so it moves against its gradient. Movement against a gradient requires an energy input, which makes this active transport. Stating the gradient direction first is what earns the point.
rationales.D: Tempts because water movement is a familiar membrane process, but osmosis is the movement of water, and the question asks how glucose crosses. Fix: describe the transport of the substance the question names.

earned: State the concentration gradient first.
Call movement against the gradient active.
Name the energy requirement and the protein involved.
lost: Calling all protein transport active.
Skipping the gradient direction.
Describing water movement when asked about a solute.

subject: AP Biology
stem: An enzyme speeds up the conversion of its substrate to product. Which statement correctly describes how the enzyme increases the reaction rate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It supplies the energy needed for the reaction to occur.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It raises the temperature of the solution so that molecules collide more often.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It binds any molecule of similar size, so it can speed up many different reactions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It binds the substrate in an active site with a complementary shape, which lowers the activation energy.

rationales.A: Tempts because a reaction 'needs energy to get started', but an enzyme does not add energy; it lowers the energy barrier that must be crossed. Fix: say 'lowers activation energy', never 'provides energy'.
rationales.B: Tempts because heat does speed up reactions, but an enzyme works at the cell's temperature and does not heat its surroundings. Fix: credit the enzyme with lowering activation energy, not with adding heat.
rationales.C: Tempts because binding the substrate is part of the right answer, but enzymes are specific: the active site fits a particular substrate by shape and chemistry, not by size alone. Fix: tie specificity to the shape of the active site.
rationales.D: An enzyme speeds a reaction by lowering its activation energy, and it does this by binding a specific substrate in an active site whose shape fits that substrate. Linking active-site shape to lower activation energy is what earns the point.

earned: Tie the active site's shape to its substrate.
Say the enzyme lowers activation energy.
Connect lower activation energy to a faster rate.
lost: Saying the enzyme adds energy.
Crediting the enzyme with heating the reaction.
Ignoring substrate specificity.

subject: AP Biology
stem: In pea plants, the allele for purple flowers (P) is dominant to the allele for white flowers (p). A plant heterozygous for flower color is crossed with a white-flowered plant. What fraction of the offspring is expected to have white flowers?

rationales.A: Tempts because 1/4 is the familiar fraction for a recessive phenotype, but it comes from crossing two heterozygotes (Pp x Pp). Fix: write both parents' genotypes before reaching for a remembered ratio.
rationales.B: The heterozygous parent (Pp) makes P and p gametes in equal numbers, and the white parent (pp) makes only p gametes. The offspring are 1/2 Pp (purple) and 1/2 pp (white). Writing both parental genotypes before the cross is what earns the point.
rationales.C: Tempts because 3/4 is the classic dominant fraction from Pp x Pp, but this cross is with a white parent, and the question asks about white offspring. Fix: set up the cross in the question, not the one you remember.
rationales.D: Tempts if you assume the dominant allele always shows up in the offspring, but the heterozygous parent passes p to half its offspring. Fix: track each parent's gametes separately.

earned: Assign each parent's genotype first.
List the gametes each parent can make.
Read the ratio from the completed cross.
lost: Using a memorized ratio for the wrong cross.
Reporting the dominant share when asked for the recessive.
Ignoring segregation of the heterozygote's alleles.

subject: AP Biology
stem: In a population in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium for a gene with two alleles, 16% of individuals show the recessive phenotype. What is the expected frequency of heterozygous individuals?

rationales.A: Tempts because pq = (0.6)(0.4) = 0.24 uses the right allele frequencies, but it leaves out the 2: a heterozygote can receive the dominant allele from either parent. Fix: the heterozygote frequency is 2pq.
rationales.B: Tempts because 0.36 is a correct Hardy-Weinberg value, but it is p squared, the homozygous dominant frequency. Fix: label each term (p squared, 2pq, q squared) before answering.
rationales.C: Tempts because 0.84 = 1 - 0.16 counts everyone without the recessive phenotype, but that group includes homozygous dominant individuals as well as heterozygotes. Fix: split the dominant phenotype into p squared and 2pq.
rationales.D: The recessive phenotype frequency is q squared = 0.16, so q = 0.4 and p = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6. Heterozygotes are 2pq = 2(0.6)(0.4) = 0.48. Taking the square root of the recessive frequency, not the dominant one, is what earns the point.

earned: Start from q squared for the recessive phenotype.
Find p from p + q = 1.
Name which term (p squared, 2pq, q squared) answers the question.
lost: Taking the square root of the wrong frequency.
Forgetting the 2 in 2pq.
Treating the dominant phenotype as all heterozygotes.

rationales.A: This is incorrect because enzymes do not supply energy. Fix: review enzyme function.
rationales.B: This is incorrect because enzymes do not change temperature. Fix: review enzyme function.
rationales.C: This is incorrect because enzymes are specific. Fix: review enzyme specificity.
rationales.D: Choice D is the correct statement about how enzymes work.

earned: Tie the active site's shape to its substrate.
Say the enzyme lowers activation energy.
Connect lower activation energy to a faster rate.
lost: Saying the enzyme adds energy.
Crediting the enzyme with heating the reaction.
Ignoring substrate specificity.

A Punnett square for one gene has four boxes.

subject: AP Biology
stem: A population of beetles lives on tree bark that darkened over several decades. Birds find light-colored beetles more easily than dark-colored ones on the dark bark, and beetle color is heritable. Which outcome is most likely over many generations?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Individual light beetles darken their color to avoid being eaten.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The frequency of alleles for dark color increases in the population.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The population stays the same because color does not affect reproduction.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Birds evolve to see dark beetles more easily within one generation.

rationales.A: Tempts because it describes an adaptation, but individuals do not change their inherited traits in response to need; populations change across generations. Fix: describe change in allele frequencies in the population, not in one individual.
rationales.B: Dark beetles survive and reproduce more on dark bark, and color is heritable, so alleles for dark color are passed on more often and rise in frequency. Linking differential survival of a heritable trait to allele frequency change is what earns the point.
rationales.C: Tempts if you overlook the link between survival and reproduction, but beetles that are eaten leave fewer offspring. Fix: connect survival to reproductive success.
rationales.D: Tempts because predators can evolve too, but evolution happens across generations, not within one. Fix: keep the timescale to many generations.

earned: Name the heritable variation first.
Link survival to reproductive success.
Describe change as allele frequency in the population.
lost: Saying individuals change their genes.
Ignoring heritability.
Compressing evolution into one generation.
